title: MEMS-fab vapor HF releases capacitor molds with no rinse water
idea: Phase shift from liquid to vapor: run the anhydrous HF/alcohol vapor release tools that are standard in existing 200 mm MEMS fabs to strip sacrificial oxide molds around capacitor pillars. There is no liquid, no rinse, no capillary collapse and no UPW.
why: Saves tens to hundreds of liters of UPW per wafer at that step, allows taller pillars and puts idle MEMS capacity to work on capacitor modules.

title: ALD alumina nano-topcoat replaces fluorinated immersion-litho topcoats
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | Si | ArF immersion]: after resist coat, grow 2-3 nm of 60 C ALD Al2O3 from TMA/H2O as the leach barrier, cap it with a fluorine-free hydrocarbon monolayer for water receding angle, and let the TMAH developer dissolve it.
why: PFAS: immersion topcoats and topcoat-free additives are fluorinated and face EU restriction; removes fluorinated chemistry from ~10-15 immersion layers per DRAM flow.

title: Point-of-use helium recapture loops on every tool
idea: Periodic-table walk, He (2): the element is irreplaceable in a few steps, so fit each remaining He user (cryopumps, leak checks, CZ purge blends) with polymer-membrane plus PSA recapture and local recompression, returning >90% to a fab ring main instead of venting.
why: Cuts virgin helium demand ~90% amid the Qatar outage (~30% of world supply offline).

title: Wartime tungsten scrap reclamation feeds domestic fab tungsten chemistry
idea: Revive 1940s cemented-carbide scrap reclamation (the zinc process) and capture tungsten from WF6 exhaust and chamber cleans, converting both into fab-grade WF6 and W targets inside the US for DUV-only memory lines.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%): closes the loop on fab tungsten; claims 50%+ of fab W from recycled sources.

title: Glass blower: refurbish quartz chamber parts instead of buying new
idea: Stimulus 'glass blower' -> a 10-person shop strips etch deposits from quartz focus rings, bell jars and furnace tubes, re-fuses eroded zones with a hydrogen-oxygen torch, fire-polishes and recertifies them, extending part life 2-4x.
why: Fab quartzware draws on the same high-purity quartz as crucibles; refurbishment roughly halves that consumption and spare-part cost.

title: Substitute rutile TiO2 on MoO2 electrodes for zirconia capacitor stacks
idea: Replace ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 capacitor dielectric with ALD rutile TiO2 templated below 400 C by a lattice-matched MoO2 bottom electrode (instead of scarce RuO2), with Al doping and a thin Al2O3 interlayer to suppress leakage.
why: Rutile k ~80-100 hits the k~70 target from the capacitor charge wall without going to AR 115; ~1.5x Cs at today's AR using only Ti, Mo and Al, removing Zr/Hf dependence.

title: One-metal cell: aluminum conductors with anodized-alumina dielectrics
idea: Ideal: one cheap material does everything. Closest: deposit a single aluminum film and convert chosen regions into dense barrier-type Al2O3 by room-temperature electrochemical anodization through a soft mask (thickness set at ~1.3 nm/V), so the same film supplies wordlines, plate electrodes and capacitor/gate dielectric.
why: Replaces W, TiN, Hf/Zr ALD and several vacuum steps with U.S.-abundant aluminum and wet benches; suits low-temperature oxide-TFT tiers; k~9 gives modest Cs but zero scarce inputs.

title: Parametron revival using MEMS-timing resonators storing phase bits
idea: MEMS timing chips (silicon resonators that replaced quartz crystals) meet Goto's 1950s parametron. Each bit is stored as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped nanomechanical resonator; one shared pump tone holds every bit, and reads use phase-sensitive detection.
why: No capacitor and no leakage tail, in all-silicon. Refresh is replaced by a continuous low-power pump, possibly ~fW per bit for high-Q resonators. Density and speed are unproven.

title: Single aluminum film anodized into lines and dielectric together
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: deposit one blanket Al film and convert the spaces between future lines into anodic Al2O3 by through-mask electrochemical anodization. One material then serves as wire, via, dielectric and pad, with no metal etch and no damascene CMP.
why: Removes Ta/TaN barriers, Co liners, W vias and Cu plating from DRAM's relaxed-pitch upper metal layers, along with several etch/CMP tools. Uses only Al, O, Ti and N.

title: Antiferroelectric zirconia biased near its field-induced transition boosts charge
idea: Combine paraelectric storage with antiferroelectric switching (zero added masks): tune ALD ZrO2 thickness and Si/Al doping so its tetragonal phase sits just below the field-induced polar transition at the storage voltage, giving an effective k ~50-60 across the operating window.
why: ~1.5x stored charge per capacitor without higher aspect ratio or hafnium, or equal charge at lower VARY (CV2 energy).

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane capacitors replace high-aspect-ratio etching
idea: Ideal: a capacitor that builds its own height. Closest: deposit a strained SiN bilayer carrying a TiN/Al2O3/TiN stack, release a sacrificial layer, and let built-in strain roll it into a 5-10-turn micro-scroll that multiplies electrode area per footprint 20-50x with no 70:1 hole etch.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (Fact 1) without HAR etch (fluorocarbon gases, etch capex) or a k~70 material.

title: Complementary SnO/ZnO sense amplifiers live inside the memory tiers
idea: Periphery is ~49% of the die because sense amps need CMOS on the substrate; p-type SnO (Sn2+ 5s hole band) plus n-type ZnO gives an oxide CMOS that deposits in the same tiers, so each tier carries its own sense/latch beside its cells.
why: Periphery falls from ~49% to ~10% with no separate CMOS wafer or bonding; with 60 tiers that is ~10x bits per die area at equal cost using Sn and Zn.

title: p-type tin-monoxide CMOS periphery stacked over the array
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sn (50): pair n-type ZTO with p-type SnO (hole mobility 1-5 cm2/Vs) to build complementary sense-amp drivers and decoders at <=400 C directly above the cell array, moving part of the 49% periphery off silicon wafer area.
why: ~25-35% less silicon wafer area per bit, hence fewer wafers, crucibles and EUV passes; Sn is abundant and already an EUV-source consumable.

title: Cryogenic helium bank filled from the fab's own exhaust
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: pipe He-bearing exhaust from leak-check stations, load locks and chuck fore-lines into a header, upgrade it with a polymer membrane, and adsorb it on activated carbon chilled by the fab's existing LN2. The fab builds a 3-6 month He buffer and releases it during supply shocks.
why: Turns helium from a just-in-time import into a buffered resource that is ~70-90% recycled, so wafer starts are insulated from events like the Qatar outage.

title: Substitute sealed nitrogen carriers for humidified ballroom cleanrooms
idea: Keep wafers in N2-purged sealed pods and tool mini-environments end-to-end so the building needs only ISO-8 air with no tight humidity control; steam humidifiers and most chilled-water coil load disappear.
why: Cleanroom make-up air is a major water (humidification and cooling-tower load) and energy user; a mini-environment-only fab cuts HVAC water >10x and HVAC energy ~50%.

title: Pharma isolator fab: sealed tool tunnels replace ballroom cleanrooms
idea: Aseptic pharma moved from cleanrooms to sealed isolators; connect DRAM tools with nitrogen-purged sealed transport tunnels and mini-environments so only ~5% of fab volume is ISO-class clean and the rest is ordinary industrial air.
why: Cleanroom air handling and makeup-air conditioning are ~30-50% of fab electricity and much of its cooling water; isolating only the wafer path could cut fab energy ~25%, water ~15% and construction cost.

title: Reusable sapphire carriers let hot-grown memory stacks laser-lift onto CMOS
idea: Thermal budget, not physics, forbids crystalline oxides above CMOS. Grow the 100-tier array stack on a sapphire carrier at 700-900 C (crystalline STO/ZnO/Si tiers), bond it face-down onto the periphery wafer, release it by UV laser lift-off as in microLED, and re-polish the carrier for ~1000 uses.
why: Unlocks high-temperature tier materials for ~10x density via 100 tiers while substrate cost per wafer approaches zero and no second CZ wafer or quartz crucible is consumed.

title: Po the chuck is a hairbrush: gas-free nanofiber thermal contact
idea: Po: 'the wafer is cooled by a hairbrush, not a gas.' Extracted: replace helium backside gas in electrostatic chucks with a dense, vertically aligned boron-nitride-nanotube or carbon-nanotube forest capped with a thin alumina skin, whose millions of compliant tips conduct heat under electrostatic clamping as well as ~10 Torr of helium.
why: Removes backside-cooling helium, one of a fab's largest helium uses, from etch, implant and CVD tools; zero per-wafer helium on those steps.

title: Nano-relay switch with vacuum capacitor: zero off-current cells
idea: Inverts 'the access device is a leaky transistor and the capacitor needs high-k': replace the access transistor with a ~50 nm electrostatic nano-relay whose open contact is a true vacuum gap (no subthreshold current) and store charge on a plain SiO2 or vacuum-gap capacitor in the same sealed cavity, so retention is set only by surface leakage (years).
why: Zero refresh power and no access-transistor leakage tail; eliminates hafnia/zirconia and Ru; contacts in TiN or conductive carbon.

title: Piezoelectric AlN nano-relays give zero-leakage access and end refresh
idea: Effect: the converse piezoelectric effect. A c-axis AlN bimorph sputtered at 300 C bends to close a Mo/TiN nano-contact, so the access device is a mechanical switch with an air-gap off-state and exactly zero subthreshold leakage. Retention is limited only by capacitor dielectric leakage (hours).
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) largely gone; AlN needs no scandium, no Si channel and no thermal budget above 400 C.

title: Getter-coated chamber walls replace helium-loop cryopumps
idea: Combine the chamber liner with the vacuum pump: sputter a TiZrV non-evaporable getter film on PVD chamber liners that pumps H2, CO and H2O at room temperature and reactivates during normal bake/seasoning, with small turbo pumps handling argon.
why: Retires helium-compressor cryopump loops and their makeup helium and ~7 kW compressors per tool; fewer regeneration downtimes.

title: Sourdough starter: reusable donor wafer feeds epitaxial DRAM layers
idea: Stimulus 'sourdough starter' (keep a mother culture, bake only a portion) -> keep a mother Cz wafer and 'bake' only a thin epitaxial slice from it. Grow a porous-Si release layer plus device-grade epi (or the Si/SiGe superlattice for 3D DRAM) on the donor, bond to a low-grade carrier, split at the porous layer, re-polish and reuse the donor 10-20 times.
why: Cuts Cz crystal pulls, high-purity quartz crucibles and polysilicon per wafer by up to ~10x; carriers can be recycled or low-purity silicon.

title: Ion-cut prime silicon films onto cast metallurgical carriers
idea: Imposed scarcity: one CZ wafer must feed ten DRAM wafers. Hydrogen-implant and split a 1.5 um prime silicon layer from a reusable CZ donor, bond it over a thin oxide-nitride diffusion barrier onto a cheap cast upgraded-metallurgical silicon carrier (made in graphite or Si3N4 molds), and build the array in the transferred film.
why: ~10x less CZ crystal and HPQ crucible per wafer; the carrier costs ~$5-10 vs ~$100+ for prime 300 mm; the buried barrier can also serve as a back-bias plane for leakage control.

title: Lower-purity specialty gases, defects absorbed downstream
idea: Reverse the spec flow: qualify 5N instead of 6N-7N grades of NF3, silane, WF6 and ammonia from a wider supplier base, and let the trace-contaminant cell defects sit inside the 1% BER budget.
why: Specialty gas purification is energy- and supplier-concentrated; widening grades cuts cost ~30% and sole-source risk.

title: Fiber-optic preform silica lines CZ crucibles, ending Spruce Pine dependence
idea: Optical-fiber makers need ppb-pure silica and synthesize it by flame hydrolysis of SiCl4 instead of mining it. Polysilicon plants produce SiCl4 as a byproduct: turn it into synthetic silica soot and sinter a 3-5 mm bubble-free inner liner onto a crucible shell made from ordinary non-Spruce quartz sand.
why: HPQ crucibles are >80% Spruce Pine: a synthetic inner layer could cut HPQ per crucible ~70% and turns a polysilicon waste stream into a strategic input.

title: Low-budget-fab block copolymers print the honeycomb capacitor array without EUV
idea: Fabs that cannot buy EUV (universities, developing nations) can use directed self-assembly. High-chi block-copolymer cylinders (PS-b-P2VP) guided by a sparse e-beam or i-line template, hardened by sequential infiltration synthesis of AlOx, print the hexagonal capacitor array at ~30 nm pitch.
why: Replaces one of DRAM's 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4) with spin-coat and bake, cutting dependence on the single EUV supplier for that layer.

title: Talbot self-imaging prints periodic memory arrays without EUV
idea: Effect: Talbot self-imaging. DRAM arrays are strictly periodic, so displacement Talbot lithography (a simple phase grating lit at 193 nm and integrated across the Talbot distance) prints pitch-halved lines and honeycomb hole arrays with no complex reticle. Self-aligned quadruple patterning then reaches array pitch, and only the periphery uses conventional litho.
why: EUV single-supplier chokepoint and 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4): the array layers move to tools at ~1/10 EUV capex with mask cost near zero.

title: Retired-server DIMM reclamation business delivering tens-of-cents-per-GB pooled memory
idea: Ideal: memory that already exists and costs nothing. Closest: buy decommissioned DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs from hyperscaler refresh cycles at scrap-plus prices, auto-test and grade them, and mount them on CXL Type-3 expander cards whose controllers remap weak rows and add stronger ECC, sold as pooled second-tier memory.
why: 100x: many PB retire each year; marginal cost is test + card + controller (~$0.05-0.15/GB at scale), ~50-100x below new-DRAM pricing, with zero new wafers, helium or tungsten. Trades +70-150 ns CXL latency, power and supply variability.

title: Pottery glaze: sol-gel synthetic silica lining on ordinary-quartz crucibles
idea: Stimulus 'pottery glaze' (a thin perfect layer on a rough pot) -> a 10-person shop sprays TEOS-derived sol-gel synthetic silica onto crucibles made from lower-grade, non-Spruce-Pine quartz and fuses it with a plasma torch into a bubble-free 1-2 mm inner liner.
why: Only the melt-contact layer needs ultra-high-purity quartz; a synthetic liner removes the Spruce Pine chokepoint for that layer at small capital.

title: Holographic interference exposes periodic storage-node arrays mask-free
idea: Holograms record perfectly periodic fringes without a mask. Because DRAM arrays are strictly periodic, expose the honeycomb storage-node and landing-pad lattice by three-beam 193 nm interference or achromatic Talbot lithography, then trim array edges with a coarse DUV exposure; the die stays a standard DDR/HBM part.
why: Removes EUV and multi-patterning passes for 1-3 array layers using commodity DUV lasers; interference tools cost ~1/20 of an EUV scanner and need no lattice photomask.

title: Rutile TiO2 dielectric templated by antimony-doped tin-oxide electrodes
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ti (22) with Sn (50): SnO2 is isostructural with rutile, so a conductive Sb:SnO2 bottom electrode templates rutile TiO2 (k~90-110) at <=350 C ALD, replacing Ru/RuO2 templates and Hf/Zr high-k; a 1 nm Al-doped TiO2 cap holds leakage.
why: Hits the k~70 target from fact 1 with Ti and Sn only: ~2x Cs at the same aspect ratio or AR 70->~35; Hf-free, Ru-free.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching grows vertical channel forests at room temperature
idea: Ideal: sculpting deep silicon with no plasma. Closest: dewet a thin Ag film (or deposit Ag through a self-assembled mask) on silicon; in HF/H2O2 at room temperature the silver sinks vertically, leaving 100:1 nanopillars at 30-60 nm pitch for vertical-channel transistors or capacitor cores, made on plastic wet benches instead of $20M+ C4F6-burning etchers.
why: 100x path: wet-bench cost per wafer-pass is ~1-5% of a HAR plasma etch and removes PFAS etch gases; with self-assembled masks, array formation cost per GB falls >=100x. Trades pillar wander, Ag contamination control and porosity.

title: Brownfield DRAM fabs on retired coal plants
idea: Imposed scarcity: no new water rights, no new transmission and no greenfield permit time. Site fabs on retiring coal plants that already hold industrial water allocations, cooling reservoirs, high-voltage interconnects and rail, and convert boiler halls into utility buildings.
why: Fab water (~10-20 ML/day) and 100-300 MW of power are often the binding permits; reuse could cut 1-2 years and ~$1B in utilities from a U.S. fab schedule.

title: Sell imperfect dies: fractional-capacity DRAM with OS bad-page maps
idea: Inverts 'every die must be perfect': ship dies with up to 10-30% failing rows or subarrays as non-power-of-two capacity parts, with a signed bad-page map in an on-module EEPROM that firmware or the CXL controller reads at boot and never allocates.
why: Raises usable bits per wafer by recovering scrapped or downbinned dies (HBM yield is down 20-30%); every recovered die saves its full share of quartz, helium, energy and water.

title: Area-selective deposition ends blanket metal plus CMP
idea: Minify metal to only where it stays: self-assembled inhibitor monolayers on dielectric surfaces make Mo/TiN ALD nucleate only in contacts and lines. This eliminates the overburden and the CMP step that today removes 80-95% of the deposited metal.
why: Cuts metal precursor use 5-10x and removes ceria slurry (rare earths, China-dominated), slurry water and pad waste on several layers.

title: Lattice-coded analog charge stores ten bits across three gain cells
idea: Thermal noise on a gain-cell node is sqrt(kT/C) ~2 mV against a ~1 V window, so Shannon allows ~8 bits per cell; drift and variation eat most of it, but coding 10 bits as one point in a 3-cell lattice (vector quantization, decoded at read) averages variation, and non-destructive reads allow verify-and-trim writes.
why: 3.3 bits/cell x 3 stacked oxide decks = ~10x bits per area at the same wafer cost; scarce material per bit falls ~10x.

title: Skull-melt Czochralski: quartz-free silicon in a cold copper crucible
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero quartz crucibles. Melt silicon in a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible where the induction field both heats and pushes the melt off the wall, so a frozen silicon 'skull' is the only contact surface; pull 300 mm ingots from that pool and use nitrogen co-doping to replace the wafer-strengthening role of crucible-derived oxygen.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine >80% HPQ chokepoint for every DRAM wafer; the skull is reused indefinitely, so crucible cost (~$1-3k per pull) goes to ~0 and oxygen-precipitate variability disappears; the cost is higher RF power per kg.

title: Fifteen ingots per crucible with continuous-feed Czochralski
idea: Magnify crucible life 10-15x: feed granular FBR polysilicon continuously during the pull and devitrify the crucible's inner wall with a barium coating, so one HPQ crucible yields 10-15 prime 300 mm DRAM ingots instead of 1-2.
why: Cuts high-purity quartz per wafer ~10x, along with puller downtime and argon per wafer; reuses solar-industry CCZ know-how for prime wafers.

title: Volatile 3D NAND: direct-tunnel charge-trap strings run as DRAM
idea: Ideal: DRAM at flash prices. Closest: build a 200+-layer 3D-NAND-style string with a 1.5-2.0 nm tunnel oxide (vs 5-7 nm) so programming is direct tunneling at ~4-6 V in ~100 ns without Fowler-Nordheim damage, giving ~1e12+ endurance; retention falls to ~1-10 s, so the array is refreshed like DRAM behind a DRAM-cache controller.
why: 100x: inherits 3D NAND's ~$0.05/GB cost structure and Si/N/O/Mo materials, ~100-200x below current DRAM pricing; trades us-class string read latency (hidden by a front cache), refresh power and an unproven endurance case.

title: Po every gas well is a helium well: fab-anchored membrane extraction
idea: Po: 'every gas well near the fab is a helium mine.' Extracted: install modular hollow-fiber membrane plus PSA skids on U.S. pipeline gas streams with only 0.1-0.5% helium, normally uneconomic, co-located near fabs in Arizona, Texas and New York, and justify them with fab waste heat and long-term offtake contracts.
why: Helium supply security: many low-helium streams are vented or ignored; fab-anchored micro-extraction could cover a fab's net make-up need from domestic gas.

title: Accommodation-engineered argon backside cooling replaces helium wafer chucks
idea: Effect: free-molecular (Knudsen) gas conduction scales with alpha/(2-alpha)*P/sqrt(M), and helium's accommodation coefficient on smooth ceramic is only ~0.3 while argon's is ~0.8-0.9. Redesign electrostatic chucks with a 3-5 um gap, nano-textured Al2O3 mesas and stronger sealing bands so Ar/N2 runs at 2-3x the pressure while staying free-molecular, matching helium heat-transfer coefficients.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline): backside cooling is one of the largest fab helium uses; target ~100% He removal on etch/deposition chucks with <15% throughput penalty.

title: Million-dollar bounty for a chokepoint-free capacitor module
idea: Within $1M/24 months: put the whole budget into staged prizes ($100k milestones, $500k grand prize) for any team that shows a DRAM capacitor module of >=5 fF at <=40 nm pitch using no He, W, Hf/Zr, PFAS or HPQ-dependent steps, verified by an independent university fab.
why: Prizes often draw 10-40x their value in outside effort, turning a tiny budget into dozens of parallel material searches aimed at the capacitor charge wall.

title: Constellation-satellite short-life qualification trims barrier and liner metals
idea: Satellite constellations fly parts qualified for 5 years, not 25, and AI-accelerator DRAM is scrapped after ~4 years. Define an 'AI-life' DRAM grade with 4-year electromigration and TDDB targets that allows thinner TaN/TiN barriers and liners, Al instead of W in periphery local interconnect, and reduced reliability guardbands.
why: Cuts Ta, Ti and W per wafer ~30-50% and removes some process steps.

title: 3D printer: printed silicon-carbide chamber parts replace quartz and yttria
idea: Stimulus '3D printer' -> a 10-person team binder-jet prints carbon preforms for etch chamber rings, liners and showerheads, then converts and densifies them to high-purity SiC by chemical vapor infiltration from silane and methane.
why: Removes high-purity quartz and yttria (rare earth) from consumable chamber kits; SiC lasts 2-3x longer under plasma.

title: High-chi block copolymers plus vapor infiltration draw 12 nm arrays
idea: Effect: thermodynamic microphase separation. A high-chi block copolymer anneals at <=250 C into 12-20 nm hexagonal dots or lines, guided by a coarse ArF graphoepitaxial template. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O at 90 C) turns one block into an AlOx hard mask for array etches.
why: EUV chokepoint and PFAS-containing photoacid generators: 3-5 array EUV exposures replaced, with every step <=250 C.

title: Aircraft-brake carbon composites become crystal puller hot zones
idea: U.S. aircraft-brake plants make carbon/carbon composites by winding PAN fiber and densifying it by chemical vapor infiltration from natural gas; use those lines for CZ heaters, susceptors, heat shields and crucible supports, replacing imported isostatic graphite.
why: Isostatic graphite comes mainly from Japan and China; C/C parts last ~3-5x longer and cut hot-zone heat loss ~15-25%, lowering crystal-growth energy per wafer with an all-domestic chain.

title: Two-phase CO2 chuck cooling replaces perfluorinated heat-transfer fluids
idea: Ideal: chillers with no exotic fluids. Closest: cool cryogenic etch chucks and chamber walls with pumped two-phase CO2 (R744) evaporating inside chuck channels (-50 C reachable), replacing Galden/Novec perfluoropolyether coolants after 3M's Novec exit.
why: Eliminates a PFAS supply chokepoint in every etch/deposition chiller; CO2 latent heat improves chuck temperature uniformity; GWP ~10,000 -> 1.

title: Eliminate plasma etch and PFAS gases: catalyst-drilled capacitor holes
idea: Define a silver nanodot catalyst array by block-copolymer self-assembly on a thick sacrificial silicon mold, then immerse in HF/H2O2 so each dot sinks vertically (metal-assisted chemical etching), drilling 15-20 nm holes beyond 100:1; build electrodes in the holes, strip the mold, and recover the silver from the bath.
why: The 60-75:1 capacitor etch burns C4F6/C4F8 (PFAS, high-GWP) in the costliest etchers; room-temperature wet drilling reaches the AR~115 that fact 1 asks for with a fraction of the capital.

title: Shockley four-layer diode revived as thyristor RAM cell
idea: Revive Shockley's 1956 four-layer diode and the abandoned 2000s T-RAM: a vertical PNPN thyristor with a capacitively coupled gate latches regeneratively and stores a bit without a capacitor, built at 40 nm DUV pitch.
why: No capacitor (fact 1), no Hf, no W pillars and no EUV; reads in under 5 ns at high current; claims SRAM-like speed in a ~8F2 DUV footprint.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM using porosified p+ silicon sacrificial tiers
idea: Box [lateral cap | lateral Si access per tier | voltage SA | 3D stacked tiers | CZ Si | all-Si epi + electrochemical porosification]: grow alternating p++ (B 1e20) and lightly doped Si epi tiers instead of Si/SiGe, then after slit etch anodize only the p++ layers into porous Si and remove them laterally, leaving suspended single-crystal channels.
why: Removes germane/Ge (China dominates refined Ge, export-licensed since 2023) from 3D DRAM, and avoids the SiGe strain-relaxation cap on tier count so >100 tiers become possible.

title: Tailings-reprocessing mindset: cold-trap and refluorinate escaped WF6
idea: Miners now reprocess old tailings for the metal left in them, and CVD-W tools likewise send most of their WF6 to the exhaust. Put a cryogenic/sorbent trap ahead of abatement to catch WF6 and WOxFy, then refluorinate the captured material with on-site F2 back into WF6 feedstock.
why: Raises tungsten utilization from ~20-30% to >70%, cutting W import need per wafer ~2-3x while W is still in the process.

title: Self-barrier CuMn bitline merges conductor and diffusion barrier
idea: Combine the bitline conductor and its TiN/WSix barrier into one Cu-0.5%Mn alloy fill; a post-fill anneal drives Mn to the dielectric interface where it forms a ~2 nm MnSiOx barrier in situ, replacing the W/TiN bitline stack (later capacitor anneals capped below ~500 C).
why: Removes bitline tungsten (China ~80%) and the barrier deposition; ~2x lower bitline resistance allows longer bitlines and fewer sense-amp stripes (~5-8% die area, periphery wall).

title: Ice-storage building cooling shifts fab chiller load off-peak
idea: Office towers make ice at night to cool by day. Add stratified chilled-water and ice thermal storage to the fab process-cooling plant, and modulate upstream polysilicon reactors and abatement heaters like aluminum smelters' 'virtual battery' potlines, shifting 15-25% of electric load into cheap off-peak or curtailed-renewable hours.
why: Lowers energy cost per bit and lets ~0.5-1 GW-class memory fabs site on constrained U.S. grids without new peak generation.

title: Idle-RAM leasing agent across colocation tenants
idea: Within $1M/24 months: ship an open-source hypervisor agent that exposes each server's idle DRAM as encrypted RDMA-backed remote swap to neighboring tenants through a spot-price market, starting in one colo with 500 servers.
why: Typical clusters strand ~30-50% of installed DRAM; renting it out displaces new-DIMM purchases with zero new materials.

title: Nickel-aluminide intermetallic buried wordlines replace tungsten below 15 nanometers
idea: At sub-15 nm widths line resistivity scales with rho0*lambda (bulk resistivity x electron mean free path), not rho0, and ordered B2 NiAl has a few-nm mean free path so its size penalty is small. Fill buried-wordline trenches with Ni/Al ALD nanolaminates and anneal to NiAl, which self-passivates with Al2O3 and needs no TiN barrier.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry from DRAM's largest W use; barrier-free fill gives ~20-30% more conductor cross-section and lower wordline RC.

title: CZTS solar lesson: indium- and gallium-free oxide channels for gain cells
idea: Thin-film PV swapped scarce indium/gallium (CIGS) for earth-abundant Cu-Zn-Sn-S. Do the same for oxide-semiconductor gain cells and vertical 3D-DRAM access transistors: amorphous Zn-Sn-O or Si-doped SnO2 n-channels replace In-Ga-Zn-O, paired with p-type SnO or Cu2O for complementary gain cells.
why: Gallium is ~98% Chinese and export-controlled and indium is a China-dominated zinc by-product; this keeps oxide gain-cell ultra-low leakage and long retention while removing both chokepoints.

title: Rhodopsin-switch resist: retinal-style photoisomerization, no fluorinated acid
idea: Vision uses retinal's cis-trans photoisomerization to change a protein's shape with no acid catalyst. Build a non-chemically-amplified resist whose side chains carry retinal- or azobenzene-like switches; once isomerized they break a hydrogen-bond network and make exposed areas soluble in aqueous developer, so no perfluoroalkyl sulfonate photoacid generator is needed.
why: Removes PFAS photoacid generators (facing EU/US restrictions) from DUV layers; the lower photospeed is acceptable on the many non-critical DRAM layers.

title: Kidney physiologist cascades rinse water through graded reuse loops
idea: Persona: a kidney physiologist, since nephrons reuse water through counter-current cascades. Meter every rinse stream's conductivity and TOC in real time and route it down a ladder: final rinse, then first rinse, then scrubbers, then cooling tower, then irrigation. Polish the top rung with on-tool EDI, so each litre serves 4-6 duties before discharge.
why: Water intensity per wafer falls 3-5x, which makes fabs viable at water-stressed U.S. sites.

title: Po hafnium falls out of reactors: naval-zirconium hafnium chain
idea: Po: 'hafnium is nuclear waste.' Extracted: hafnium is separated only when nuclear-grade zirconium is made, so contract U.S. nuclear zirconium producers to convert their hafnium byproduct directly into HfCl4 and amide precursors at home, and qualify capacitor stacks that accept mixed Hf/Zr feed (HZO-like) so unseparated, cheaper feedstock works.
why: Hafnium and precursor import dependence: a captive U.S. chain from existing nuclear Zr plants; accepting mixed Hf/Zr skips the costly separation step for dielectric use.

title: Zero-kerf laser slicing: thinner wafers on reusable carriers
idea: Magnify wafers per ingot ~2.5x: split ingots along a laser-modified subsurface plane (zero kerf) into 300 um wafers, temporarily bonded to reusable carriers for processing, instead of wire-sawing 775 um wafers and losing ~150 um of kerf each.
why: DRAM dies are thinned below 50 um anyway, so over 90% of today's wafer becomes slurry. Silicon, polysilicon energy and crucible quartz per bit fall ~2.5x.

title: Hibernation zoologist: server memory that sleeps with the grid
idea: Persona: a zoologist who studies hibernation. With non-volatile main memory, whole racks drop to zero power in seconds and resume instantly when renewable supply returns. Datacenters then follow solar and wind curves and sell demand response instead of holding batteries and diesel.
why: Energy input: less firmed power is needed, along with fewer Li and Pb UPS batteries, and the 16-33% idle refresh power disappears.

title: Wound-film memory: roll-to-roll TFT DRAM coiled like a film capacitor
idea: Ideal: memory sold by the meter. Closest: imprint and print oxide-TFT DRAM arrays on 10 um aluminum/polyimide web at ~10 m/min, wind the web into a cylinder like a metallized-film capacitor, and connect every turn's wordline/bitline buses at the web edges via flame-sprayed 'schoopage' end metallization plus laser-cut edge decoders into parallel banks.
why: 100x: R2R processing ~$2-10/m2; a 1 m x 1000 m roll at 50-100 GB/m2 holds 50-100 TB for ~$10k -> ~$0.1-0.2/GB. Trades volume (a can-sized multi-TB brick), latency and thermal limits.

title: Antimony-tin-oxide electrodes template rutile TiO2 high-k capacitors
idea: Box [rutile TiO2 cap, k~90 | Si access | voltage SA | pillar stack | CZ Si | thermal ALD]: use ALD SnO2:Sb, which is conductive and rutile-structured, as the bottom electrode so ALD TiO2 crystallizes directly as rutile below 400 C instead of low-k anatase; a 0.5 nm Al2O3 interlayer at the top electrode suppresses leakage.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k~70) plus Hf/Zr/Ru intensity: k~90 vs ~40 lets aspect ratio fall from ~70:1 to ~35:1 at equal Cs, halving deep-etch time and fluorocarbon use, with no Ru (the usual rutile template) and no Hf.

title: Copper-nanodot catalyzed chemical etching drills capacitor molds
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: self-assembled Cu nanodots sink into silicon in HF/H2O2, each locally catalyzing dissolution beneath itself, so they drill holes of 100:1 or deeper at room temperature without plasma. The silicon mold is then oxidized or lined to form the capacitor template.
why: Replaces the most capital-heavy, fluorocarbon-hungry step (high-aspect-ratio mold etch) with a wet bath: ~10x lower tool capital and no C4F8/CF4. Uses only Cu, Si, H, O and F.

title: Twistor revival: helical-anisotropy Fe-Al nanowire memory, platinum-free
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1957 twistor: electroplate an Fe-Al (Alfenol) or NiFe shell on copper nanowires while a mismatched coaxial stress layer applies torsion, locking in a helical easy axis. Bits are helical magnetization segments switched by coincident wire current and an orthogonal copper strap, and read inductively along the same wire, so no MTJ stack is needed.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: removes the Pt/Ir/Ru/Ta layers of MRAM and the Hf/W of DRAM; magnetic storage gives unlimited endurance and zero refresh energy (fact 3); claims a 30-60 ns cycle with ~10x less scarce metal per bit.

title: Cofactor plasticity: recipes that swap tungsten, molybdenum or ruthenium
idea: Archaea swap W and Mo into the same enzyme scaffold depending on what the environment offers. Qualify every DRAM metal fill (wordline, contacts, bitline plugs) as a family that can run W, Mo or Ru in the same ALD chamber with a shared barrier and anneal, so a fab can switch metals within weeks as prices or embargoes move.
why: Hedges the W chokepoint and eases a move to Mo (lower resistivity in narrow lines, US-mined) without a full requalification each time.

title: Plated-wire NDRO cells on copper bitlines, read without destroying data
idea: Revive 1960s aerospace plated-wire memory: electroplate a 20 nm NiFeCo sheath with circumferential anisotropy around damascene copper bitlines in BEOL, with aluminum word straps crossing over. A word pulse tilts the sheath magnetization without flipping it, so the sign of the induced bitline voltage gives the bit non-destructively. Aqueous plating at <80 C needs no W, no high-k and no fluorinated etch.
why: Destructive read and 128x overfetch (fact 8): only addressed bits are sensed and nothing is restored; avoids W, Hf and PFAS etch gases; nonvolatile, so no refresh; claims ~3x lower read energy per useful bit.

title: Eliminate charge pumps: monolayer MoS2 access transistors driven from 1 V
idea: Replace the buried silicon access device with a gate-all-around monolayer MoS2 channel (U.S. molybdenum, refinery sulfur) whose ~2 eV gap and 0.7 nm body give near-zero off-current at 0 V, so the wordline swings 0-1 V straight from VDD with no VPP pump or negative-wordline supply.
why: Wordline energy drops (3 V/1 V)^2 times ~2.5x avoided pump loss, ~20x; also removes the leakage tail behind refresh (fact 3) and the pump area.

title: Electromagnetic cold-crucible Czochralski eliminates Spruce Pine quartz entirely
idea: Replace the fused-quartz crucible with a segmented, water-cooled copper cold crucible. An RF field heats the silicon and partly levitates it, and the melt freezes a thin silicon skull against the wall, so molten silicon only ever touches silicon. Scale jump from vessel to field: Lorentz force and a self-grown shell do the containing.
why: Removes the >80%-concentrated HPQ crucible chokepoint and yields ultra-low-oxygen silicon with fewer leakage-inducing precipitates. Energy per kg rises ~30-50% unless cusp magnetic fields cut heat loss.

title: Sinclair's audio RAM revived: sell partially good DRAM with defect maps
idea: 1980s ZX Spectrums used half-defective 64k DRAM ('ARAM'), a market that vanished as yields rose. With HBM yields down 20-30%, sort dies with failed banks, burn a signed defect map into an eFuse page, and let accelerator memory controllers or CXL expanders skip dead banks for KV cache and activations.
why: Every scrapped die is sunk helium, quartz, tungsten, water and energy; recovering half the fallout lifts usable supply ~10-15% with zero new materials or capex.

title: Eliminate dissipative bitline charging: stepwise adiabatic charge from idle-bitline tanks
idea: Charge the active bitlines in 8-16 small voltage steps, using idle neighbouring bitline groups as charge reservoirs (stepwise adiabatic charging), and return the charge in reverse steps at precharge so resistive CV2 loss drops by the step count.
why: Bitline sense/restore is the largest slice of activation energy; 8-16 steps cut it ~8-12x using the existing array as the tank, with no inductors or added capacitor material.

title: Termite-mound stack-effect cleanroom air handling
idea: Termite mounds ventilate passively with a tall chimney, thermal mass and porous walls. Build the fab with a process-heat chimney that drives make-up and return air by buoyancy, earth-tube preconditioning and phase-change thermal mass, so fans only top up the flow through the ULPA ceiling.
why: HVAC is ~40-50% of fab electricity; passive buoyancy and thermal mass could cut it 20-35%, lowering energy intensity and allowing fabs on weaker grids.

title: Qimonda deep-trench DRAM revived with polysilicon and oxynitride only
idea: Revive the trench-capacitor DRAM abandoned with Qimonda (2009) and IBM eDRAM: deep substrate trenches with doped polysilicon electrodes, an oxide-nitride dielectric and buried-strap access, built on 28-40 nm ArF immersion lines in US foundries.
why: No EUV, no Hf/Zr and minimal tungsten, on existing US mature capacity; claims US DRAM output from existing fabs within 2 years, at ~3x the cost per bit of the leading edge.

title: Vertical charge-coupled shift strings: memory without per-bit transistors
idea: Ideal: memory with no transistor, capacitor or contact per bit. Closest: in a 3D-NAND-like stack, clock tier wordlines three-phase so charge packets move along a vertical oxide-semiconductor channel like a CCD; each string is a shift register read by one sense amp at its foot, with a regeneration stage every ~32 tiers to cancel transfer loss.
why: 100x: deletes the cell capacitor, contacts and leakage tail (Facts 1-3), uses only Si/O/N/Mo, and scales density with tier count at ~3D-NAND cost (~$0.05/GB). Trades serial access (~100-300 ns per 64-stage shift, hidden by bank interleaving) and charge-transfer efficiency.

title: Dry-cleaner supercritical CO2 replaces water rinses after etch
idea: Adapted from dry cleaning's switch from perchloroethylene to supercritical CO2. Strip post-etch polymer residue and dry high-aspect structures in scCO2 with small co-solvent doses, with the CO2 recycled through a separator and compressor; with no surface tension, tall pillars cannot collapse.
why: Cuts UPW and IPA in the many post-etch cleans (~20-30% of fab water) and removes the yield loss from capacitor-pillar leaning at 60-75:1 aspect ratios.

title: Soviet reverse-engineer rebuilds UltraRAM from silicon and oxide
idea: Persona: the classic Soviet copy of a Western design built from domestic materials. Replace UltraRAM's InAs/AlSb triple-barrier resonant-tunnelling stack with Si/SiO2 double barriers around a silicon quantum well. Electrons tunnel resonantly into a floating gate at ~2-3 V, and off resonance the barrier blocks leakage for years.
why: Non-volatile charge storage with low-wear, fast writes from Si and O only, with no In, Sb or Ga. Endurance target 1e12.

title: Keyboard snap-dome physics as a contactless bistable nanobeam bit
idea: Keyboard snap-domes and pressure-relief discs use buckled shells with two stable states. Adapt this as a pre-stressed silicon-nitride nanobeam per bit that snaps up or down under electrostatic pulses and is read without contact through piezoresistive strain or a MOS gate underneath.
why: No capacitor, no leakage path and no refresh, using only Si and SiN (no Hf, W or In). A contactless snap avoids stiction, so endurance could exceed 1e15, and GHz-scale nanobeams switch in ~1-10 ns.

title: Display-glass fabs make oxide-transistor memory on Gen 8.5 panels
idea: Worsen: insist that every DRAM bit needs a 300 mm single-crystal wafer from a CZ puller with a quartz crucible. Flip: repurpose underused LCD/OLED fabs to build stacked oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on 2.2x2.5 m glass (~60x the area of a 300 mm wafer) with their existing PVD/ALD and litho tools, and bond the logic periphery from silicon fabs.
why: Quartz/polysilicon intensity and capital: display fabs are depreciated and overbuilt, with cost per area ~10-20x lower. Density is low, so this targets a stacked capacity tier.

title: Rebreather-style closed helium loop for etch and ALD chucks
idea: Adapted from closed-circuit diving rebreathers, which scrub and recirculate expensive heliox instead of venting it. Each tool gets a foreline tap that captures backside-cooling helium leaking past the e-chuck (plus leak-check station exhaust), strips it through a getter cartridge and cold trap, and recompresses it into the chuck supply loop.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline since March 2026). Fabs vent almost all backside He; 85-95% per-tool recapture cuts purchased helium ~5-10x and buffers spot shortages.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling retrofit for etch chucks
idea: Within $1M/24 months: in a university fab, retrofit a used 300 mm etcher's electrostatic chuck to run H2 backside gas at ~10 Torr (no O2 present, so no ignition path), with Pd-getter cleanup and leak interlocks, and map wafer temperature against He.
why: H2's thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) exceeds He's (~0.15), so cooling is equal or better while removing the largest per-wafer helium use; H2 can be made anywhere.

title: Memory-as-a-service: makers keep ownership and take modules back
idea: Worsen: sell DRAM outright, so makers profit from short lives and scrap. Flip: makers lease memory capacity to data centers by the GB-month, keep ownership, and take modules back for re-binning, repair and redeployment, so durability becomes the maker's profit lever.
why: Usable supply per wafer and capital intensity: each fabricated bit serves 2-3 deployments.

title: Eliminate quartz furnace tubes: flash-lamp and microwave anneals
idea: Replace batch diffusion and anneal furnaces (high-purity quartz tubes and boats) with millisecond flash-lamp and volumetric microwave anneals in single-wafer chambers for dopant activation, dielectric crystallization and passivation.
why: Removes recurring Spruce Pine quartzware demand and long furnace thermal cycles; less dopant diffusion also helps the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: N+1 spare core die with TSV bypass crossbar in HBM
idea: Worsen: make every die in a stack a single point of failure. Flip: add one spare core die and a programmable TSV crossbar in the base die. A die that fails at test or in the field is fused out and its channels remapped to the spare, repairing the stack in place.
why: HBM stack yield and field life: a spare die costs ~8% against 20-30% stack scrap, and deployed life gets longer.

title: Xenon-anesthesia recapture logic for every rare gas in fab exhaust
idea: Hospitals recapture exhaled xenon anesthetic with cryogenic adsorbers because Xe is so scarce, yet fabs dump Ne, Kr and Xe from lasers, implanters and etchers. Fit point-of-use pressure-swing/cryo-adsorption cartridges that capture rare gases before dilution and regenerate them centrally to 99.99%.
why: Cuts neon, krypton and xenon purchases ~70-90%, defusing a war-exposed chokepoint.

title: Adiabatic resonant wordline drivers recycle charge, reviving 1990s reversible computing
idea: Revive 1990s adiabatic switching (Younis/Knight) for DRAM periphery: drive wordlines and plate lines from shared on-die LC tanks with slow sinusoidal ramps, so each activation's charge returns to the tank instead of being dumped to ground.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): recovers 50-70% of the 3 V wordline CV2 energy, and energy is a scarce data-center resource; needs no new materials.

title: Refinery side-draws: U.S. steel-plant air separators harvest neon
idea: Oil refineries pull extra fractions from column side-draws; add crude rare-gas columns to the big air separation units at U.S. steel mills and chemical plants, purify neon, krypton and xenon centrally, and recycle the fab's ArF/KrF laser exhaust through the same plant.
why: Neon (once ~50% from Ukraine and Russia) gates DUV lithography; a domestic supply plus laser gas recycling secures every exposure in a U.S.-only, no-EUV DRAM flow that relies more heavily on multipatterning.

title: Si-only Esaki tunnel-diode latch replaces the DRAM capacitor
idea: Revive TI's 1990s tunneling SRAM, descended from Esaki's 1957 diode: stack two delta-doped, silicon-only interband tunnel diodes (no germanium) on the storage node of a single access transistor. The negative-differential-resistance pair latches the node at two stable voltages, giving a static cell with pA-level standby current and no capacitor.
why: Removes the high-aspect-ratio capacitor (fact 1), its ZrO2/HfO2 and its TiN/W electrodes, and refresh (fact 3); claims a static cell with a 1T footprint of ~8F2.

title: Skip hafnium-zirconium separation: qualify natural-ratio zirconium precursors
idea: Combine the two elements nature already combines: electronics needs no nuclear-grade Hf/Zr separation, so qualify ALD precursors made directly from unseparated zircon (~2% Hf) for ZrO2 capacitors and specify periphery dielectrics as natural (Zr,Hf)O2.
why: Deletes the costly solvent-extraction separation step (a large share of precursor cost) and makes hafnium non-critical for DRAM.

title: Intel 1103 three-transistor cell rebuilt in indium-free zinc-tin oxide
idea: Revive the 1970 Intel 1103 3T dynamic cell in BEOL-stacked amorphous zinc-tin-oxide transistors, with no indium and no gallium. The wide bandgap gives ultra-low off-current, so the gate node holds charge for seconds and the gain transistor reads it non-destructively.
why: The prior work's IGZO depends on indium and gallium, both concentrated in China, while ZTO uses Zn and Sn; the gain read removes the capacitor (fact 1), slashes refresh (fact 3) and stacks over the periphery (fact 7).

title: Meteorite-collecting alien builds MRAM from cosmic iron-nickel
idea: Persona: an alien who knows meteorites. Use tetrataenite (L1_0-ordered FeNi, Ku ~1 MJ/m3) as the perpendicular free and reference layers of MTJ cells. Make it on-wafer by nitrogen insertion and topotactic extraction (FeNiN to FeNi), forcing the ordering that nature needs millions of years to reach.
why: Non-volatile MRAM with unlimited endurance and no cobalt, platinum, palladium or rare earths. Fe and Ni are abundant and can be sourced in the U.S.

title: Silica-lined polyethylene replaces fluoropolymer ultrapure-water piping
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: build UPW and chemical distribution from high-density polyethylene pipe whose inner wall carries a plasma-deposited SiOx/a-C:H barrier film. The film blocks leaching and particle shedding, the reasons PFA/PVDF (both PFAS) were chosen.
why: Removes PFAS fluoropolymers from the fab's largest-volume wetted plastics ahead of PFAS restrictions. Uses only C, H, Si and O.

title: Wurtzite AlBN ferroelectric cell: hafnium-free, nonvolatile DRAM
idea: Inverts 'ferroelectric memory needs hafnia or lead': sputter wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N from abundant Al and B in N2 as the cell capacitor's ferroelectric in a 1T1C array whose sense amps read polarization-switching charge (remanent polarization >100 uC/cm2, ~5x HZO).
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; the huge polarization lets a planar or shallow capacitor replace 70:1 pillars, cutting etch gas and mold; no Hf, Zr or Pb, and AlN is already a US-made MEMS material.

title: Silaffin-peptide biosilica as synthetic crucible-grade quartz
idea: Copy diatoms: silaffin-mimetic polyamine peptides (or cheap long-chain polyamines) precipitate amorphous silica at room temperature and neutral pH from silicic acid made by dissolving ordinary US industrial sand in base and purifying it by ion exchange first. The biosilica is sintered into the inner layer of fused-silica crucibles, so purity comes from solution chemistry instead of rare pegmatite quartz.
why: Attacks the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz chokepoint for Cz crucibles; any sand becomes feedstock at ppb metal purity, decoupling crucible supply from one county.

title: Gecko-setae thermal pads replace helium backside wafer cooling
idea: Gecko feet make intimate contact through millions of compliant setae. Hot-emboss roll-to-roll a replaceable chuck-top film of copper-flake-filled polyimide micro-pillars that conform to the wafer backside under electrostatic clamping and carry heat by solid contact instead of helium gas.
why: Eliminates helium backside cooling in etch and CVD, one of the biggest fab helium uses, with pads made by the kilometre as cheap consumables.

title: Watchmaker's click spring: snap-through nanomechanical bistable memory
idea: Persona: a watchmaker who relies on bistable click springs. A pre-stressed SiC or SiN nanobeam buckles either up or down, the two stable states. An adjacent electrode snaps it electrostatically and a capacitive sensor reads it, with no contact or stiction.
why: Non-volatile mechanical memory with no wear limit, made of Si, C and N. Leakage is essentially zero and ~10 ns switching is possible.

title: Fully silicided titanium wordline grown inward from polysilicon fill
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: instead of depositing metal into the buried-wordline trench, fill the trench with doped polysilicon and convert it in place, top-down, into C54 TiSi2 (Ti deposition, Si pre-amorphization, two-step RTA). The conductor is grown from what is already there.
why: Removes W, WF6 and the TiN liner from the array. TiSi2 (~15 uOhm-cm bulk) approaches W at these widths, survives ~850 C and uses only Ti and Si.

title: Space-station water recovery chain for 95% ultrapure-water reclaim
idea: Adapted from the ISS water recovery system: vapor-compression distillation, multifiltration beds, catalytic aqueous-phase oxidation and conductivity-gated reject loops. Segregate rinse streams by contamination class at every wet bench and run each class through a modular distillation and catalytic-oxidation skid that returns water to UPW polishing.
why: Fabs draw ~10+ ML/day of water and typically reclaim 40-70%. A 95% closed loop cuts intake ~5x and makes fabs viable in arid US sites (AZ, TX, NM).

title: Eliminate stored zeros: zero-line bitmaps keep sparse tensors off DRAM
idea: The controller keeps a 1-bit-per-64-byte zero map in on-die SRAM; all-zero lines and zero-dominant lines (run-length encoded) are never written to or read from the DRAM array.
why: ReLU-sparse activations, pruned weights and optimizer states with 50-90% zero lines see 2-10x fewer accesses, >10x on the sparsest tensors, and freed capacity.

title: Half-voltage arrays: trade sense margin for quartered energy
idea: Reverse the margin budget: drop VARY from ~1 V to ~0.5 V and wordline boost proportionally, let ~1% of cells fall below sense margin, and correct them with ECC.
why: Breaks the voltage floor on energy, a facet input: CV^2 array energy falls ~4x, cutting memory power and the fab-to-datacenter energy footprint.

title: Bond a mature-node periphery wafer under the array
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: move sense amps, decoders and I/O (~49% of the die) to a separately processed 28-40 nm CMOS wafer that is hybrid-bonded beneath the cell array. The array wafer then needs no Hf-based HKMG and fewer metal layers.
why: Raises bits per array wafer ~1.6-1.9x, removes Hf HKMG from the array fab, and lets periphery run in existing U.S. mature-node fabs (capital and U.S. manufacturability).

title: Undo the helium reserve sell-off: a chip-grade helium strategic stock
idea: The U.S. sold its Federal Helium Reserve (completed 2024), so Qatar's 2026 outage hit fabs with no buffer. Re-create a fab-dedicated stock: require 80-90% recapture of chuck-backside and leak-check helium (membrane plus cryogenic recovery) and bank recovered surplus and U.S. field helium in the Cliffside storage under a strategic-stock lease.
why: Helium is small in mass but irreplaceable for wafer cooling; recapture plus a reserve gives multi-year cover against single-region outages that otherwise cost weeks of DRAM output.

title: Zero-ballroom fab: wafers travel in sealed nitrogen tubes
idea: Minify the cleanroom ~100x: connect tools with sealed N2/vacuum wafer highways and keep ISO-1 air only inside tool mini-environments, so the building is a cheap warehouse instead of a filtered ballroom.
why: Cleanroom HVAC is ~40-50% of fab energy. Fab energy falls ~50%, makeup water and capital per wafer start fall too, and US fabs go up faster.

title: Avogadro-sphere isotopic silicon-28 epi cools hot HBM stacks
idea: The kilogram redefinition and spin-qubit research use centrifuge-enriched silicon-28, which carries heat better without isotope scattering. Grow the HBM base-die and core-die device epi from 28SiH4 enriched in repurposed gas centrifuges, improving lateral heat spreading inside the stack while the HBM interface stays standard.
why: HBM refresh doubles above 85 C; ~10-15% better silicon conductivity plus thinner dies trims hotspot temperature a few degrees, delaying the 2x-refresh regime and its energy at the same pins.

title: Resistless patterning via UV-written monolayers and selective ALD
idea: Worsen: depend on fluorinated photoacid generators and PFAS surfactants in every resist and developer. Flip: coat a self-assembled monolayer inhibitor, write the pattern by DUV-induced decomposition of the monolayer, and grow the hard mask by area-selective ALD only where the monolayer is gone, skipping resist coat and develop.
why: PFAS phase-out risk and resist supply concentrated in Japan: removes resist chemistry and track tools on non-critical layers, ~20-30% fewer chemicals per layer.

title: Retention-binned salvage turns reject dies into usable capacity
idea: Time-scale binning: dies that fail the 64 ms retention screen because of a few weak rows are profiled per row. The map is stored in module SPD flash, and the controller refreshes weak rows at 16-32 ms while the rest run at 256 ms.
why: Recovers ~3-8% of existing wafer output that is scrapped today and cuts refresh energy on the strong rows, all from existing fabs.
